name: Burg Berneck
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Berneck perches dramatically on a sheer schist cliff 130 meters above the Faggenbach gorge at the entrance to the Kaunertal.
preis: Exterior viewing free; guided interior tours in summer approx. €6.00 to €8.00
oeffnungszeiten: Exteriors viewable year-round; guided tours available July to September on selected days
beschreibung:
Overview

Spectacularly positioned Burg Berneck (also known as Schloss Bernegg) clings to a steep slate precipice at an elevation of 1,076 meters above the village of Kauns at the gateway to the Kaunertal. Regarded as one of North Tyrol's most audaciously sited medieval fortresses, the stronghold towers more than 130 meters vertically above the roaring Faggenbach gorge. Documented as early as 1225, this clifftop castle guarded the strategically vital transit corridor leading over the Finstermünz and Reschen passes into Italy for centuries. After centuries of neglect, Innsbruck architects Rolf and Waltraud Kathrein spearheaded a meticulous historic restoration starting in 1976 that saved the complex from ruin. Today, Burg Berneck shines as a masterfully preserved gothic fortress with reconstructed living quarters, ramparts, and a late-gothic chapel.

Route & Requirements

The castle stands on the eastern edge of Kauns and is easily reached on foot from the village center in about 15 minutes along a paved lane. As the castle sits on an exposed promontory above the canyon, visitors prone to vertigo should take care, although all public areas and defensive walls are protected with wrought-iron railings. Comfortable leisure shoes are adequate for the visit. Due to spiral staircases, narrow gothic doorways, and uneven cobblestones, the interior is not wheelchair or stroller accessible. Families with children are welcome, though young children should be supervised near precipices. From the battlements of the keep, breathtaking views extend across the entire Kaunertal, the Upper Inn Valley, and Laudegg Castle near Ladis.

Visit & Arrival

Burg Berneck is privately owned and opens its doors during the summer months (approx. July through September) for guided historical tours on scheduled weekdays (usually Friday afternoons or by advance booking through the Kaunertal tourist office). The exterior and viewing terraces can be admired year-round from outside. Motorists travel via the A12 and B180 to Prutz, turn toward Kaunertal, and follow signs up to Kauns (parking in village center). By rail, travel to Landeck-Zams and take the public bus via Prutz to Kauns.

Tips

Join the guided tour to admire the restored gothic frescoes in Saint Bartholomew's Chapel and the impressive knight's hall. Pair your excursion with a walk along the historic Kauner Waalweg irrigation channel or to the nearby Naturparkblick observation platform.
